question.text: The equation of the plane passing through the point of intersection of the lines <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mn>1</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo></math> <math><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac></math> and perpendicular to the line <math><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></math> is <math><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo></math> If the distance of the point <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>1,1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> from <math><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> is <math><mi>k</mi></math> units, then the value of <math><mfrac><mrow><msup><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></math> is equal to

solution.text:
Any general point on the line x-13=y-21=z-32 is 3λ+1,λ+2,2λ+3
For the point of intersection, this point must satisfy the line x-31=y-12=z-23
⇒3λ-21=λ+12=2λ+13⇒λ=1
So, point of intersection is 4,3,5
The required equation of plane is
2x-4+3y-3+1z-5=0
⇒2x+3y+z-22=0
Hence, the distance of the plane from 1,1,3 =2+3+3-2214=14=k
